manifest.research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
sources.evidence_checked: arXiv record and full-text HTML v3

exact_overlap.user_next_item_behavior: YES — explicitly trains a Transformer sequence-to-sequence model on Semantic IDs in a user session to predict the Semantic ID of the next item the user will interact with.
exact_overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: NO — the accessible abstract and full-text framing describe semantic codeword tuples and generative retrieval, not hyperbolic geometry.
exact_overlap.generative_semantic_ids: YES — creates semantically meaningful tuples of codewords as item Semantic IDs and autoregressively decodes target identifiers.

sources.relevance: Strong evidence for next-item user behavior plus generative Semantic IDs, but not for the hyperbolic component.

sources.title: Time-aware Hyperbolic Graph Attention Network for Session-based Recommendation
sources.evidence_checked: arXiv record abstract; full text not independently inspected

exact_overlap.user_next_item_behavior: YES — abstract defines session-based recommendation as predicting users' next interested items from previous browsing sessions and describes prediction based on timestamp.
exact_overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: YES — proposes a time-aware hyperbolic graph attention model and learns hierarchical session graphs in hyperbolic space.
exact_overlap.generative_semantic_ids: NO in the checked abstract — no generative retrieval or Semantic IDs are described.

sources.relevance: Directly relevant to behavior-first next-item modeling and hyperbolic session representation; does not establish generative Semantic IDs.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Hypergraphs for Sequential Recommendation
sources.evidence_checked: arXiv record abstract; full text not independently inspected

exact_overlap.user_next_item_behavior: PARTIAL — sequential recommendation with multi-scale temporal item embeddings is explicit, but the checked abstract does not state the precise next-item target in those words.
exact_overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: YES — uses hyperbolic-space hypergraph convolution to learn dynamic item embeddings.
exact_overlap.generative_semantic_ids: NO in the checked abstract — no generative retrieval or Semantic IDs are described.

sources.relevance: Adjacent evidence for sequential behavior and hyperbolic representation, not the generative-ID intersection.

sources.title: HMamba: Hyperbolic Mamba for Sequential Recommendation
sources.evidence_checked: arXiv record abstract; full text not independently inspected

exact_overlap.user_next_item_behavior: PARTIAL — explicitly addresses sequential recommendation and dynamic interaction sequences; checked abstract does not specifically assert Semantic-ID next-item decoding.
exact_overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: YES — proposes curvature-aware hyperbolic selective state-space sequence modeling.
exact_overlap.generative_semantic_ids: NO in the checked abstract — no Semantic IDs or generative retrieval are described.

sources.relevance: Recent hyperbolic sequential-recommendation comparator; it does not document generative Semantic IDs.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Social Recommender
sources.evidence_checked: arXiv record abstract; full text not independently inspected

exact_overlap.user_next_item_behavior: NO explicit next-item prediction in the checked abstract; evaluates click-through-rate prediction and top-K recommendation.
exact_overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: YES — models user/item representations and social relations in hyperbolic geometry.

sources.relevance: Background on hyperbolic recommendation only; not evidence for the requested full intersection.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Behavior-conditioned next-item generation with hierarchical (hyperbolic) Semantic-ID structure
behavior_problem_candidates.grounding: Combine the explicitly observed user-session-to-next-Semantic-ID task in Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval (FULL_TEXT) with the hyperbolic session/sequence modeling direction in TA-HGAT and HMamba (ABSTRACT).
behavior_problem_candidates.evidence_status: SYNTHESIS / research gap, not a method already verified in one source
behavior_problem_candidates.behavior_first_question: Does representing item-ID hierarchy in a negatively curved space improve prediction of the user's next interacted item from their observed session, compared with Euclidean Semantic IDs, while retaining autoregressive decoding?

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Temporal intent evolution and branching next-item choices in short sessions
behavior_problem_candidates.grounding: TA-HGAT's abstract explicitly identifies temporal intervals/current interests and next-interested-item prediction; H2SeqRec's abstract describes multi-timescale sequence modeling and dynamic social information.
behavior_problem_candidates.evidence_status: SYNTHESIS / candidate problem framing; no checked source tests these behaviors with generative Semantic IDs
behavior_problem_candidates.behavior_first_question: Which temporal transitions or session-intent branches are lost when the next item is represented by a flat code sequence, and can hierarchical geometry improve behaviorally valid branching?

behavior_problem_candidates.grounding: Generative Retrieval reports improved retrieval for items with no prior interaction history in its abstract; hyperbolic recommendation abstracts motivate hierarchy/long-tail structure. Their combination remains unverified.
behavior_problem_candidates.evidence_status: SYNTHESIS / candidate; avoid claiming the combined effect is established
behavior_problem_candidates.behavior_first_question: Do generative Semantic IDs plus hyperbolic structure improve next-item prediction for rare or unseen items without reducing accuracy on frequent-item behavior?

limitations: No independently verified source among those checked demonstrates all three elements together: user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative Semantic IDs. The evidence supports two-element overlaps and a research gap, not an existing integrated result.
FULL_TEXT is assigned only to the arXiv Semantic-ID paper whose experimental HTML was accessible and inspected; the other labels indicate abstract-only evidence, not full-text verification.
Negative claims are scoped to the evidence inspected (primarily abstracts); they do not prove a term or technique is absent from every version or appendix.
arXiv-issued DOI is provided for Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval. For the remaining entries, arXiv identifiers are supplied and DOI is null rather than guessed.
The behavior problem candidates are proposed synthesis from the cited evidence, not claims made or validated by those papers.
